_: Channel summaries, generated. Keyed by repo, then a hash of the channel's source notes + tools/release-notes-prompt.md + the model (see channel_key in sync-releases.py). Written by tools/summarize-notes.py in the GitHub Action (model = the Claude model that wrote it) or by hand (model "hand"). Edit "bullets" freely: an entry is kept until its channel's notes change. "fold": true adds the closing "Plus smaller fixes and polish" line. An entry with "failed" is ignored by the page and asked again after 7 days; delete it to try sooner. Keep this file valid JSON: while it does not parse, nothing is summarized.

bullets: **Image generation** — ask for a picture and you get one; FLUX.1 schnell runs on your Mac, or a cloud model fills in
Model downloads show real progress, and name what is actually downloading
**Enable visual effects** now switches only the moving backdrop, not spinners and animations
**Check for updates automatically** is yours to choose: at launch and once a day, or never
**Windows** — chat, web search, read-aloud and voice input on Intel, AMD and ARM PCs; the app installs Ollama for you
**Video** — ask for a short clip and your Mac renders it; a size ladder shows what each quality setting costs
**Export to twenty formats** — ask for an answer as a PDF, Word document, spreadsheet, slides, calendar file or CSV
**Models that stay current** — newer versions offered after each update, and the right cloud model once a cloud key is added
Live weather answers and giant models for 512 GB+ systems; **Removed** — Contribute and the free community image cloud
**Backdrops follow your clock** — dark clips from sunset to sunrise where you are, and no more lean toward New York
**First-run setup** — builds your server on DigitalOcean end to end, or takes your own server's keys; NextDNS is optional
**Automatic speed test** in Performance mode — waits for a verified exit, and re-runs when the network changes
**Settings** is a proper dialog, with an update channel (stable, beta or nightly) and **Flush the DNS cache**
**Updates** — offered in their own dialog with Skip, and About shows what's new in each build
**Kill switch** — while the tunnel is up, nothing gets around it, and its self-test tells blocked from broken
Performance and Ultra race every transport and use the fastest one
**Full test** — measures your line first and says whether the VPN or the line is the limit
**Settings** in five sections — your own bypass list, speed limits set by you or on auto, and OS updates for your servers
The Direct row is back at the top of Auto's tests, and stays there after a relaunch
